chains.title: C250T creates a stronger GABPA/ETS site that activates TERT

links.claim: The alt allele at TERT promoter C250T creates or strengthens an ETS-family motif, and GABPA binds the alt allele more strongly than the ref allele.
C250T lies in the TERT core promoter and acts as an allele-specific ETS-responsive regulatory element.
The alt allele increases TERT promoter activity and TERT transcription.
This mechanism is relevant in glioblastoma cells, the provided expression context, and plausibly in melanoma and bladder cancer where TERT promoter mutations occur.
Increased TERT/telomerase activity supports telomere maintenance, cell immortalization, and tumor growth in glioblastoma.

predictions: Allele-specific GABPA ChIP at the TERT promoter enriches the alt allele over the ref allele.
GABPA knockdown reduces TERT expression preferentially in C250T-heterozygous glioblastoma cells.
A TERT promoter reporter carrying C250T shows higher activity than ref, and this difference is GABPA-dependent.
falsified_if: Allele-specific GABPA ChIP shows no alt-allele enrichment.
GABPA knockdown does not reduce TERT expression or reporter activity.
The C250T reporter effect persists unchanged after GABPA depletion.

chains.title: C250T is not itself the TF-mediated causal variant
predictions: No allele-specific TF binding at C250T distinguishes ref from alt.
TERT expression is driven by a linked causal variant, a passenger mutation at a mutational hotspot, or another non-allelic mechanism.
C250T reporter alleles show no differential activity, or any difference is not TF-dependent.
falsified_if: Allele-specific ChIP or EMSA demonstrates reproducible alt-allele enrichment for a specific TF.
Depletion of that TF reduces the C250T allele-specific reporter or TERT expression effect.

chains.title: C250T creates a stronger ETS1 site that activates TERT

links.claim: The alt allele at TERT promoter C250T creates or strengthens an ETS-family motif, and ETS1 binds the alt allele more strongly than the ref allele.
C250T lies in the TERT core promoter and acts as an allele-specific ETS1-responsive regulatory element.
The alt allele increases TERT promoter activity and TERT transcription.
This mechanism is relevant in glioblastoma cells and possibly in melanoma and bladder cancer.
Increased TERT/telomerase activity supports telomere maintenance and tumor growth.

predictions: Allele-specific ETS1 ChIP at the TERT promoter enriches the alt allele over the ref allele.
ETS1 knockdown reduces TERT expression preferentially in C250T-heterozygous glioblastoma cells.
GABPA ChIP does not show stronger alt-allele enrichment than ETS1 ChIP.
falsified_if: Allele-specific ETS1 ChIP shows no alt-allele enrichment.
ETS1 knockdown does not affect TERT expression or reporter activity.
GABPA, not ETS1, is the dominant allele-specific factor at this site.
